summary_md:
**Everything in `customer.yaml` is a guess except where noted.** No UK lender or broker has been quoted yet (research: 'Not found'), so segments, shares, incomes and behaviours are my reading of the bet's Who plus the research. Only the objections are grounded: Crediflow's existing source-traced memo generator, vendor-feed substitutes (Codat, Equifax, Ocrolus), price, and the NACFB count are from the research; the rest are inferred from the open questions D3, D4, D5.

**Check before dealing buyers:**
1. **Segment shares (D2/D10/D16).** I put brokers at 0.40, analysts at 0.35 and heads of credit at 0.25, but the bet has not chosen one buyer. If you pick lenders only, drop the broker segment and re-split the shares.
2. **Incomes** are rough UK salary or owner-draw ranges, not sourced.
3. **Behaviour shares** are guesses. The 'loyal to existing data vendor' and 'keeps Excel plus Word' behaviours rest on D3 and the research's open-banking substitutes.
4. **Price in `pitch.md` (£1,200 for a 5-memo assessment) is a placeholder with no evidence behind it.** The only list prices found are Codat at £25 per company per month and an Equifax rate of about £3 per connection, and neither is a memo price. Set the real figure, or leave it, since the bet's test is whether anyone names a price band.
5. **Pitch deliverability.** It promises a memo as a document with every figure cited and a named human approver. It promises no UI, which fits the non-goals. Confirm you can deliver 5 memos in the time stated, and that D7 (employment contract and data-protection terms) lets you offer this at all.
6. **The Crediflow objection is real**, since it is in the research. The pitch deliberately makes no uniqueness claim.

files.customer.yaml:
business: Credit memo service for UK SME lending. Takes 12 months of business current-account statements and returns a memo in which every figure is calculated deterministically, cited to its source transactions, and approved by a named human before release.
target: Credit analyst or head of credit at a UK non-bank SME lender (about 10-50 staff), or the packager at an NACFB commercial-finance broker, who spreads 12 months of statements before a memo is written.
segments:
  - name: Broker director or packager at an NACFB firm (GUESS - may not spread at all; many forward statements raw, see D2)
    share: 0.40
    income: [45000, 130000]
  - name: Credit analyst at a 10-50 person non-bank SME lender (GUESS)
    share: 0.35
    income: [40000, 65000]
  - name: Head of credit / credit director at a non-bank SME lender (GUESS)
    share: 0.25
    income: [70000, 120000]
behaviours:
  - name: Keeps Excel plus Word
    share: 0.20
    how: Spreading and the memo are the analyst's own judgement. They will not hand that over and will say the current way works (GUESS, D3).
  - name: Loyal to a data vendor already in the stack
    share: 0.20
    how: Already gets categorised transactions from Codat, Ocrolus, Equifax Share by Bank or the loan system, and asks why add another tool (GUESS, D3; the vendors are in the research).
  - name: Tries it free on one real file first
    share: 0.20
    how: Pays nothing until a memo for a deal they already know matches their own numbers; a free demo costs them nothing, so interest is not intent (D6).
  - name: Waits for a peer reference
    share: 0.15
    how: Wants to hear that another UK lender uses it. Crediflow already names UK customers, so this buyer asks you for yours.
  - name: Small fixed-fee tester
    share: 0.15
    how: Will pay a modest one-off fee for a few memos if it needs no integration and no procurement, charged to a team budget they control.
  - name: Buys only after an audit or funder finding
    share: 0.10
    how: Moves only when a warehouse funder, guarantee-scheme audit or credit committee has asked where a figure came from (GUESS, D4/D13; no case found).
objections:
  - "Crediflow already fills our own memo template with source traceability and has UK lender customers. What do you do that they do not?"
  - "We already get categorised transactions from our open-banking or data vendor. The memo is the part we write ourselves."
  - "Which of our people checks the figures, and who is accountable if one is wrong?"
  - "No regulator or funder has asked us where a figure came from, so why pay for citations?"
  - "You are one person with no track record. What happens to our files if you stop trading?"
  - "Where does our applicants' statement data go, and what is your legal basis for holding it?"
  - "I cannot see a price anywhere. Vendors in this space say contact sales, and the ones with prices look expensive per file."
  - "My broker packs are sales documents and the lender redoes them anyway."
habits:
  - Opens statements as PDFs and builds a spreadsheet by hand before writing the memo in Word.
  - Learns about tools from NACFB events, trade press and peers, not from cold email.
  - Checks a figure by searching the statement for the transaction.
  - Sends the memo to a credit committee or senior colleague for sign-off before a deal proceeds.
notes: "GUESSES: every share, income range and behaviour, because no UK lender or broker has been quoted (research 'Not found'). Grounded in research: the Crediflow, data-vendor and price objections, and that 1,400 is roughly the NACFB member count (1,414 in Jan 2026), not firms found spreading by hand. Segment shares assume the bet has not yet picked one buyer (D2/D10/D16); if it does, drop the others and re-split to 1."
files.pitch.md:
A credit memo built from 12 months of a business's current-account statements, delivered as a document.
Every figure in it is calculated by fixed rules, not written by a language model, and carries a citation to the statement lines it came from.
A named person on your side reviews and approves the memo before it is released. It does not make or replace the credit decision.
Price: £1,200 fixed for an assessment of 5 statements (placeholder, not yet tested with any buyer).
To get it: send anonymised statements by secure upload; memos come back as documents, with no software to install.
Opening offer: the first memo is free, on a statement you have already written up yourself, so you can compare the figures.
